* * *
 JUDGMENT This claim petition is filed under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, claiming compensation of Rs.20,00,000/ from the respondents on account of the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a Road Traffic accident that occurred on 23.8.2018.

2. It is the case of the petitioner that on 23.8.2018 at about 8.45 p.m., when she was travelling slowly and steadily in front of Veerasandra signal Petrol bunk, Hosur service road, Bengaluru, on her Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA51EZ5740, at that time the driver of Canter bearing Reg.No.KA51 A1898 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner, without caring for human safety and thereby dashed against the petitioner's vehicle.

Due to this SCCH23 3 MVC No.5777/2018 impact,
the petitioner fell down and sustained injuries all over her body.

Hence she was taken for treatment to Sparsh & Blossom hospitals, wherein Xrays were taken, fracture was detected and the doctors opined that the petitioner should be operated as the injuries are grievous in nature.
Though the petitioner has taken best available treatment, she is still suffering from disability.
That she has spent more than 2 lakhs towards hospitalization and other incidental expenses.
She was working as a Fashion designer and earning a sum of Rs.25,000/ p.m.
Due to the accident she has lost all her income.
In fact the petitioner was the sole bread earner in her family and all her family members were dependant on her for their food, clothing and shelter.
That the petitioner was hale and healthy at the time of accident.
However due to the accident she not only lost all her income but has also suffered lot of physical and mental stress.

The first respondent being the insurer and the second one being the owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to her along with interest @ 12% p.a.
3.
Second respondent was placed exparte.
First respondent/Insurance company resisted the claim petition SCCH23 4 MVC No.5777/2018 by filing written statement.
It denied the petition averments in toto.

Inter alia contended that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties namely the owner of two wheeler bearing No.KA51EZ5740 and its insurer as the alleged accident took place on account of head on collision between the two wheeler bearing No. KA51 EZ5740 and Canter bearing Reg.No.KA51A1898.
In fact asserted that the said accident occurred on account of sole negligence on the part of the driver of Two wheeler bearing Reg. No.KA 51EZ5740.

The Insurance company however admitted the issuance of policy to the Canter bearing Reg.No.KA51 A1898 vide policy No.2315/56254107/02/000 valid from 17.6.2018 to 16.6.2019,
but disowned its liability.
Further specifically claimed that the Investigation Officer failed to forward the copy of the report of accident to the jurisdictional claim Tribunal and also to it as required u/s 158(6) of IMV Act.
Under these circumstances prayed to dismiss the petition with costs.

sentences.text: 2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation ?

If so, to what amount and from whom ?
3. What Order or award?
5.
During evidence, the petitioner got herself examined as P.W.1.
Ex's.P1 to P9 were marked.
Dr.Nagaraj B.N S/o Late B.K.N.Swamy, Orthopaedic surgeon & Medico Legal Consultant at Sparsh Hospital Team, Bengaluru, was examined as PW.2 and Ex.P10 & 11 were marked through this witness.
On the other hand, respondent No.1 did not choose to adduce evidence.
6. Oral arguments were addressed on both sides.
Perused the entire materials placed on record.

My answers to the above issues are as follows: Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue No.2: Partly in the affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order for the following SCCH23 6 MVC No.5777/2018 REASONS 7. ISSUE NO.1: The case of the petitioner is that she sustained injuries in a RTA which took place on account of the negligence of driver of the Canter in question.

It is significant to note that to claim compensation for the injuries sustained due to the actionable negligence of a tort feasor, it is a sine qua non to demonstrate the factum negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Initial burden is on the petitioner.
To discharge the same, petitioner filed affidavit evidence reiterating the petition averments.
In support of her ocular evidence she has relied on Ex's.P.1 to 9.

Ex.P1 is the FIR registered by the Electronic city Traffic police station against the driver of the Canter in question for the offences punishable u/s 279, 337 of IPC and u/s 134(a) & (b), 187 of IMV Act, on the basis of complaint (Ex.P2) lodged by the petitioner's brother.

Ex's .P4 & 6 are the Spot Mahazar and Rough sketch prepared by the police, wherein the topographical situation of the place of accident and the exact spot of impact respectively are narrated and depicted accordingly.
Ex.P5 is the IMV report, wherein it is mentioned that the impugned accident had not occurred due to the mechanical defects of the vehicles involved SCCH23 7 MVC No.5777/2018 therein.
Further the damages suffered by the said vehicles are also set out.
Ex.P7 is the final report filed by the jurisdictional police against the driver of Canter bearing Reg.No.KA51A1898 by opining that the accident took place on account of his negligence.

Ex.P3 is the wound certificate which discloses that on 24.8.2018, due to accident the petitioner sustained (i) Right ankle bimallelolar fracture and (ii)
Cut lacerated wound on right leg , both of which are grievous in nature.
Ex.P8 is the notarized copy of the Petitioner's DL. 7 medical bills amounting in total to Rs.17,404/ are exhibited at Ex.P9.

During the cross examination of PW.1 it was suggested to her that as per the MV report no damages were found on her vehicle, which she denied and voluntarily stated that there were scratches on her two wheeler.
It was also suggested to her that it was she who hit the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
PW.1 not only denied the said suggestion but also volunteered to state that in reality the Canter hit her two wheeler.

8. In its written statement the respondent No.1 specifically contended that the alleged accident took place on account of head on collision of the two vehicles viz., Two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA51 EZ5740 & Canter bearing SCCH23 8 MVC No.5777/2018 Reg.No.KA51A1898.

But the recitals Vinothini Rajvel vs Universal Shampo General on 24 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150131798/
3 of Ex.P5 make it evident that there was no head on collision between the aforesaid vehicles as fresh visible scratch marks were found on the right panel sheet of the petitioner's Honda Activa, whereas the Ashok Leyland Canter had sustained no damages to it.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Had it been a head on collision, obviously both the vehicles would have suffered damages on their anterior portion, which is not the case.
No doubt as per Ex.P5 no visible damages were found on the offending Canter.
But just because no damages were caused to the Canter, it cannot be concluded that it was not at all involved in the accident.
Furthermore pleadings without proof are of no value.
That is to say the first respondent/Insurance company did not lead rebuttal evidence to prove its defence as taken up in the written statement.
Even in the cross examination of PW.1 nothing worth mentioning was elicited from her mouth to prove that the accident involving its insured vehicle had not occurred due to the fault of its driver.
The contents of the police documents as discussed supra have not been denied or disputed by the respondent No.1.

Hence by applying the principle of Preponderance of probabilities this Tribunal SCCH23 9 MVC No.5777/2018 concludes that the offending Canter dashed against the vehicle of the petitioner and caused the accident.

9. In addition to this in a claim for compensation u/s 166 of MV Act 1988, the claimant has to prove the accident only on Preponderance of probabilities and Standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required, as per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in a decision reported in 2011 SAR (Civil) 319 between Kusum & Others V/s Sathbir and others.

entities.text: Kusum & Others V/s Sathbir and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
The relevant portion of the afore cited decision is culled out as under:
"It is well known that, in a case relating to Motor Accident Claims, the claimants are not required to prove the case, as it is required to be done in a Criminal Trial.

The Court must keep this distinction in mind".
10.

Reference in this connection may also be made to the decision of the Apex Court in AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others) , wherein it has been held that in a Road accident, the strict principles of proof as in a Criminal case are not attracted.

entities.text: AIR 2009 SC 2819 (Bimla Devi & others V/s Himachal Road Transport Corporation & others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Relevant portion of the said decision is reproduced as follows:
SCCH23 10 MVC No.5777/2018 "15.
In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular Bus, in a particular manner, may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of Proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied".
Discussion supra manifests that the accident took place due to the negligence of driver of the offending Canter, which resulted in injuries to the petitioner.
With this observation issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
11. ISSUE NO.2 : PW.1 deposed that due to accidental injuries she suffered disability and incurred considerable medical and incidental expenses.
Therefore, prays to award compensation.

As already discussed above, the petitioner had proved that the accident took place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle and therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation.

AGE, AVOCATION AND INCOME:
Petitioner has not produced any document to demonstrate her age.
In the absence of proof, the age of petitioner as shown in the medical records is taken into consideration, wherein her age is indicated as 23 years.
To substantiate her contention that she is working as a Fashion Designer and earning Rs.25,000/ p.m, petitioner has not put in any efforts at all.
In the absence of proof, the income of the petitioner is considered as Rs.9,000/ p.m, on the basis of notional income (as the accident occurred in the year 2018).
Needless to mention, also taking into consideration the age of the petitioner and her nature of work.
PW.1 has deposed that on account of accidental injuries she has become disabled and prays to award compensation.

In this backdrop the just & reasonable compensation is awarded to the petitioner under the following heads:
13.
ATTENDANT CHARGES, EXTRA NUTRITIOUS FOOD & CONVEYANCE CHARGES:
The Case sheet of Sparsh hospital marked at Ex.P10 reveals that the petitioner was inpatient therein for about about 5 days.

As such during her stay in the said hospital,
SCCH23 12 MVC No.5777/2018 having regard to the grievous injuries sustained by her, she unavoidably required the service of an attendant for nursing and care.
She must also have been given diet food as suggested by doctor.

For that, petitioner and her family members might have spent some amount towards attendant charges, food,
nourishment and travelling expenses.
No documentary evidence can be expected for the expenditure incurred in respect of the same.
Taking into consideration the factors stated supra, this Tribunal awards a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head to the petitioner.

14. PAIN & SUFFERINGS:
The Wound certificate, Case sheet & Xrays produced at Ex's.P3, 10 & 11 show that the petitioner has sustained following injuries in the said accident: (i) Right ankle bimallelolar fracture and (ii) Cut lacerated wound on right leg .
As per the medical records said injuries are grievous in nature.
The OPD record of Sparsh hospital which includes the Discharge summary discloses that the petitioner took treatment in the said hospital from 24.8.2018 to 28.8.2018.
Considering these aspects, she is entitled for Rs.20,000/ towards Pain and Sufferings undergone by her.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING LAIDUP PERIOD:

PW.1 sustained Right ankle bimallelolar fracture and took treatment as an inpatient for 5 days.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained and the line of treatment it can be said that the petitioner might have required atleast 2 months to recover from the same.
Therefore during such laidup period, she lost income.
Hence a sum of Rs.18,000/ (Rs.9,000 x 2) is awarded under this head.
16. MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The petitioner has produced 7 medical bills at Ex.P9 amounting to Rs.17,404/ in total.
When the same are scrutinized in detail it is found that the 1 st bill of Rs.1,800/ is issued by Sri.Brahmalingeshwar Upahar towards food charges.
The same would not come under purview of medical bill and thus is not considered.
Even otherwise the petitioner is already awarded just compensation under the head of Attendant charges, extra nutritious food & conveyance charges.

Further the 3 rd bill is an advance receipt issued by Blossom MultiSpeciality hospital (where the petitioner took initial treatment) on 23.8.2018 which is already included in the final bill SCCH23 14 MVC No.5777/2018 produced at Bill No.7.
Hence Rs.6,120/ is taken twice for calculation by the petitioner.
Bills No.4 & 5 pertain to Sparsh hospital (Rs.5,100/ in total i.e., Rs.5,000/ towards advance receipt & 100 towards OPD registration).
However it is relevant to state that the final bill of the said hospital is not produced.
Considering bills No.2 , 6 & 7, petitioner is awarded a sum of Rs.10,000/ under this head.
17. LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME DUE TO DISABILITY:
It is the specific case of petitioner that owing to accidental injuries she became disabled and lost her earning capacity.

Therefore she examined Dr.Nagaraj B.N S/o Late B.K.N.Swamy, Orthopaedic surgeon & Medico Legal Consultant at Sparsh Hospital Team, Bengaluru, as PW.2 who has deposed that the petitioner was treated with Open reduction & Internal fixation with CC screws for the medial malleolus and ORIF with plate & screws for the distal fibula.
He has assessed the disability of the petitioner as follows: Physical disability of right lower limbs37% , whole body disability 12%.
This witness admitted in the course of his cross examination that the fractures are SCCH23 15 MVC No.5777/2018 united and the restriction of movement is only at right ankle joint.
He also admitted the suggestion that he has not shown description and reasoning in support of mobility & stability components of the disability stated.
Further it was also elicited from his mouth that the whole body disability stated at 12% is not a permanent disability.
18. From the line of cross examination, it is also noticed that the disability has been assessed before the removal of implants.
In fact the disability should be assessed after the completion of full treatment.
If the doctor had done so, the percentage of disability would not have been so much.
Therefore I am of the opinion that the disability assessed by the doctor is excessive.

sentences.text: Be that as it may, it is well known that loss of earning capacity is to be determined based upon the permanent physical impairment.
Pw.1 has not convincingly established her avocation.
She stated that she is working as a Fashion designer.
If it is really so then she uses her lower limbs to the minimum extent.
Considering the nature of injury, line of treatment and evidence of medical officer it can be said that the whole body disability assessed at 12% is on a higher side.
Looking into the avocation of PW.1, it can be SCCH23 16 MVC No.5777/2018 said that the disability affects her occupation to the extent of 4% .
According to medical records Pw.1 was aged 23 years at the time of accident.
As per Sarla Verma's case the appropriate multiplier applicable is '18'.

In this background petitioner is entitled for Rs.77,760/ (9,000 X 12 X 18 X 4/100) under this head which is rounded off to Rs.78,000/.
19. LOSS OF FUTURE AMENITIES AND HAPPINESS:
At the age of 23 years the petitioner has suffered 12% physical disability to her whole body and has to lead the rest of her life with such disability.
Hence I award a sum of Rs.20,000/ to the petitioner under this head.
20. FUTURE MEDICAL EXPENSES:
The doctor has deposed in his evidence affidavit that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of implant which would cost around Rs.40,000/ in a private setup.
However he admitted that he has not produced estimation for removal of implants.
Admittedly the fact that implants were inserted near the right ankle joint of the petitioner is not in dispute.
But the sum of Rs.40,000/ as quoted by SCCH23 17 MVC No.5777/2018 the doctor for removal of implants is at a higher end.
Awarding Rs.10,000/ under this head would meet the ends of justice.
However the said amount shall not bear any interest.

4 Medical Expenses : 10,00000 5 Loss of future income : 78,00000 due to disability 6 Loss of future :
20,00000 amenities & happiness 7
Future medical : 10,00000 expenses Total 1,66,00000 22.
REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY:
Respondent No.2 is the owner & respondent No.1 is the insurer of the vehicle bearing Reg.KA51A1988.
The SCCH23 18 MVC No.5777/2018 respondent No.1 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to indemnify the RC owner.
The respondent No.1 has admitted the policy coverage of offending Canter.

For these reasons they are jointly and severally liable to pay the aforesaid award amount together with interest @ 9% p.a. (except on Rs.15,000/ awarded under the head of Vinothini Rajvel vs Universal Shampo General on 24 November, 2020 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150131798/
7 future medical expenses), from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount to the petitioner.

SCCH23 19 MVC No.5777/2018 23. ISSUE NO.3:

In view of the discussion made supra in issues No.1 and 2, this Tribunal proceeds to pass the following;
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec. 166 of M.V Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

The petitioner is entitled to get compensation of Rs.1,66,000/ (Rupees One lakh Sixty six thousand only) with interest at the rate of 9% p.a. (excluding future medical expenses) from the date of petition till its deposit.
The respondent No.1 is liable to pay and directed to deposit the compensation amount within a period of one month from the date of award.
After deposit, the entire compensation amount together with interest shall be released to the petitioner on proper identification and verification.

SCCH23 20 MVC No.5777/2018 In the matter of disbursement of award amount together with interest, the office shall follow the guidelines issued by the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka in MFA No.2509/2019 (ECA), vide orders dated 19.7.2019 in the case of Smt.Yamuna Channabasappa Shetty V/s K.Raghukumar @ Raghu S/o Kotrappa.
